brief: Small caps are selling off as Treasury yields surge, with the Russell 2000 down about 8% since mid-August and now testing its long-term trend line and 200-day moving average, a make-or-break technical zone. The author had flagged three days earlier that the lower-quality, more rate-sensitive segment of the market would take the hit, and Russell's latest leg lower has tracked the yield surge closely. As 10-year yields rise, IWM keeps losing ground to QQQ, and IWM just posted its largest weekly outflows since March. The selloff carries a vol anomaly: bond volatility (MOVE) has jumped on the ugly price action, but Russell 2000 volatility (RVX) has barely budged and remains dull, even though Russell has otherwise traded in lockstep with the inverted MOVE. The note's thesis: if the rates move turns disorderly, small-cap vol is unlikely to stay this quiet, making Russell vol a cheap hedge against contagion from the rates-driven equity selloff.
